articles.title: Uber Confirms Data Breach – Hackers Stole Users’ Personal Information
articles.summary:
Uber has confirmed a data breach involving the personal information of thousands of U.S. drivers after hackers accessed records held by Fireworks AI, a third-party technology provider. The exposed information includes driver’s license details. Uber is notifying affected people, but it has not disclosed the total number impacted nationwide. The incident became known to Uber […]

The post Uber Confirms Data Breach – Hackers Stole Users’ Personal Information appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: New TypoPrompting Attacks Turn Mistyped AI Website Addresses Into Malware Installation Traps
articles.summary:
A simple typing mistake can now cost you more than a failed page load. Researchers have found that mistyped addresses of popular AI tools lead to fake verification pages, hidden commands and malware installers. The technique is called TypoPrompting. The research traced 186 lookalike domains across 27 AI brands, including Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Midjourney, […]

The post New TypoPrompting Attacks Turn Mistyped AI Website Addresses Into Malware Installation Traps appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: Hackers Use SANSAR Linux Malware to Hide Crypto Mining by Faking 0% GPU Usage
articles.summary:
Hackers are hiding cryptocurrency mining on Linux GPU servers by changing the readings administrators use to spot heavy workloads. The toolkit combines a Rust-based controller called SANSAR, a kernel rootkit, and a modified NVIDIA monitoring library that reports 0% GPU utilization while mining continues in the background. The intrusion reached three Linux GPU hosts through […]

articles.title: Hackers Use 2,700 Passwords to Break Into Microsoft SQL Servers and Deploy Remote Access Malware
articles.summary:
A new campaign is guessing its way into internet-facing Microsoft SQL Server systems. The attackers use a list of more than 2,700 passwords and then install a cryptocurrency miner and a remote access trojan (RAT) on the hacked machines. The campaign has been running since at least early October 2026. Database servers hold valuable data, […]

articles.title: Citrix Patches 28 Security Vulnerabilities in NetScaler, Including a Critical Flaw in Default Installations
articles.summary:
Citrix has released fixes for 28 security flaws in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. One of them, CVE-2026-120868, affects every deployment in its default setup. Cloud Software Group published bulletin CTX697305 on November 12, 2026, and rated it Critical. CVE-2026-120868 is a memory overflow in packet processing. It carries a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.3. […]

The post Citrix Patches 28 Security Vulnerabilities in NetScaler, Including a Critical Flaw in Default Installations appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: Hackers Use Fake Purchase Order Emails to Deliver XLoader Malware Through Malicious Word Documents
articles.summary:
Hackers are sending fake purchase order emails to trick recipients into opening Word documents that deliver XLoader, an information-stealing malware. The attack uses an embedded document, an old Microsoft Equation Editor vulnerability, and several script stages to reach its final payload. What begins as a routine order confirmation can end with stolen browser data and […]

articles.summary:

Microsoft confirmed that connectivity problems could affect users in any region, expanding the scope beyond its initial investigation into Exchange Online mailbox access in the Americas. articles.title: Hackers Use DeepSeek and GLM AI Agents to Breach 10 Organizations in Autonomous Cyberattacks
articles.summary:

articles.summary:

articles.summary:
